title: Unauthorized Registration
description: Homeowner (EE1) can register an account without proper authorization or verification, potentially allowing unauthorized access to the Home Hub's data.
assumptions: No explicit authorization mechanism is described for the registration process.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if registration includes any verification step.

title: Inappropriate Data Collection
description: Homeowner (EE1) may enroll cameras/sensors without explicit consent or understanding of the data being collected.
assumptions: No explicit consent mechanism is described for the enrollment process.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if enrollment includes any consent mechanism.

title: Unauthorized Process Execution
description: Home Hub (P1) may execute processes (e.g., data processing, analytics) without proper authorization or oversight.
assumptions: No explicit authorization mechanism is described for the processing steps.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if processing steps include any authorization mechanism.

title: Guest User Access Code Leakage
description: Guest User (EE2) enters a temporary access code at the Home Hub (P1). If the code is not encrypted or is transmitted over an unsecured channel, it may be intercepted or logged, revealing the user's identity and intent to access the front door.
assumptions: The guest user is not authenticated or the access code is not protected.
uncertainty_note: Assuming the guest interaction is unauthenticated and the code is not encrypted.

title: Home Hub Data Leakage
description: The Home Hub (P1) may inadvertently leak information about the guest user's access code or the fact that a guest is present, potentially revealing the user's identity or intent to access the front door.
assumptions: The guest user is not authenticated or the access code is not protected.
uncertainty_note: Assuming the guest interaction is unauthenticated and the code is not encrypted.

title: Unauthorized Access to Home Hub
description: An unauthorized user or process could access the Home Hub (P1) and read sensitive motion/door/sensor data before it is written to the Local Event Log (DS1).

title: Data Exfiltration via Home Hub
description: An unauthorized user or process could exfiltrate sensitive motion/door/sensor data from the Home Hub (P1) to an external entity or another process.

title: Unauthorized Access to Local Event Log
description: An unauthorized user or process could access the Local Event Log (DS1) and read sensitive motion/door/sensor data.

title: Data Exfiltration via Local Event Log
description: An unauthorized user or process could exfiltrate sensitive motion/door/sensor data from the Local Event Log (DS1) to an external entity or another process.

title: Unauthorized Access to Uploaded Clips
description: Process P1 (Home Hub) may expose camera clips to unauthorized users or entities without proper authorization checks.
assumptions: No explicit authorization mechanism is described for the upload process.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if authorization checks are implemented or if the process inherently allows unauthorized access.

title: Data Leakage to Cloud Storage
description: Process P1 may leak sensitive camera clip data to the external DataStore (DS2) without encryption or access controls.
assumptions: No mention of encryption or access controls for the upload operation.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if data is encrypted in transit or at rest when moving to DS2.

title: Data Disclosure: Home Hub Exposes Motion Alerts
description: The Home Hub (Process P1) forwards real-time motion alerts to the Mobile App Backend (Process P2). According to the mapping table, valid interactions include Process->Process. This flow represents an explicit disclosure of personal data (motion alerts) from a process to another process. If the motion alerts contain personal data, this constitutes a Data Disclosure threat (Dd) as it involves the transfer of personal data across a boundary.
assumptions: The motion alerts contain personal data.
uncertainty_note: Assumption made based on the flow description stating 'real-time motion alert' being forwarded. If the alert is generic system status rather than personal data, this threat may not apply.

title: Data Disclosure: Mobile App Backend Receives Motion Alerts
description: The Mobile App Backend (Process P2) receives real-time motion alerts from the Home Hub. This process acts as a data receiver in the flow. If the alerts are personal data, the backend is involved in the transfer of personal data, which can be classified as a Data Disclosure threat (Dd) depending on the specific context of the alert's content and the backend's role in processing or storing it.
assumptions: The motion alerts are personal data.
uncertainty_note: Assumption made based on the flow description stating 'real-time motion alert' being forwarded. If the alert is generic system status rather than personal data, this threat may not apply.

title: Unauthorized Access to Motion Data
description: The mobile app backend (P2) may expose motion-detected data to the homeowner (EE1) without proper authorization or encryption, potentially allowing the homeowner to access private health or movement information.
assumptions: The backend system is accessible to the homeowner's device.

title: Data Leakage to Unauthorized Source
description: The homeowner (EE1) may inadvertently or intentionally share their motion-detected notification with unauthorized parties, such as family members or third parties, who are not part of the system.
assumptions: The homeowner has access to the notification and may share it.

title: Data Leakage
description: Mobile app backend (P2) shares aggregated device-usage analytics with the cloud analytics vendor (EE3). This represents a potential data leakage risk where sensitive user data is transmitted externally.
assumptions: The backend process is configured to transmit all aggregated analytics data to the vendor without additional filtering or masking.

title: Data Leakage
description: The cloud analytics vendor (EE3) may share aggregated device-usage analytics with the mobile app backend (P2). This represents a potential data leakage risk where sensitive user data is transmitted back to the internal system.
assumptions: The vendor's data export settings allow full transmission of analytics data to the backend process.

title: Violation of storage limitation principle
description: The video clip stored in DataStore (DS2) is retained for a duration longer than necessary for the homeowner to play it back, constituting a violation of the storage limitation principle.
assumptions: The video is stored indefinitely or for an extended period beyond the specific timeframe required for playback.

title: Unauthorized processing of personal data
description: The mobile app backend (P2) processes the video clip (personal data) without explicit authorization or a valid legal basis, potentially violating privacy rights.
assumptions: The app has no explicit consent or legal basis for processing the video clip.
